title: Named-root binding path flattens Engram transport failure evidence (EOF/deadline, PID, observed exit) into a generic bad_gateway string
outcome: When an Engram request on the named-root binding or source-root path fails, the user-visible and recorded error keeps the structured causal failure the transport captured: EOF vs deadline, PID, observed exit state and unknown application outcome. An over-budget reply is reported with that structure instead of a generic "reply arrived after its budget". The exact pending intent and key and the unknown outcome are preserved, with no blind write retry.
acceptance: When an Engram request on the named-root binding or source-root path fails, the surfaced and recorded error keeps the transport's structured causal failure: EOF vs deadline, PID and generation, observed exit state, and unknown application outcome. It is not flattened into a generic bad_gateway string. An over-budget reply carries that structure instead of a generic 'reply arrived after its budget'. Tested.

For every supervised Engram child (identified by PID and generation), TermAl keeps a durable record of either its observed exit code or the host's own kill/termination reason. The record survives cleanup, includes the phase of any active or queued request, and never labels a process observed running at EOF as a proven crash, nor host cleanup as the original cause. Tested.
The exact pending intent and key and the unknown outcome are preserved, with no blind write retry. No raw request, token or panic prose is logged. Tested.
